java.label: Basic Solution
java.code: public static int countWordsInASentence(String input) { return Arrays.stream(input.trim().split("\s+")).filter(word -> !word.isEmpty()).toArray().length; }
java.note: Good to try: this is readable and compact, but the stream chain is usually less explicit than the cleaner loop-based explanation when the interviewer wants exact control.

java.label: Alternative
java.code: public static int countWordsInASentence(String input) { String[] words = input.trim().split("\s+"); return words.length == 1 && words[0].isEmpty() ? 0 : words.length; }
java.note: Best: this keeps the core idea simple and readable without overcomplicating the logic.

java.label: Loop
java.code: public static int countWordsInASentence(String input) { int count = 0; for (String word : input.trim().split("\s+")) { if (!word.isEmpty()) count++; } return count; }
java.note: Good to try: the explicit loop is easy to reason about, which makes it a strong backup when the interviewer wants to see every step.

java.label: Stream API
java.code: public static int countWordsInASentence(String input) { return Arrays.stream(input.trim().split("\s+")).filter(word -> !word.isEmpty()).toArray().length; }
java.note: Good to try: this is concise and elegant, but it is usually a second-choice answer unless the problem is clearly built for a collection pipeline.
